_note: The RS17's sound, for the game's sound (audio/dsp.js; docs/AUDIO.md): every file it plays and how. layers: loops at rpm points from idle to the redline (idle, low, mid, high, redline), each on load (throttle open) and off load (shut); the game plays the nearest rpm point, crossfading to the next over the middle of the gap (blend, by log rpm), and on / off load by the throttle (load: from … fully on); each plays at rpm ÷ its own rpm, so the loudest loop is never more than about 15% off its own pitch (the points are about 29% apart; a quieter one crossfading in or out, about 19%). mix: how loud at the redline on load (level), and at idle and off load as shares of that; the level rises as (rpm / redline)^curve, so it's louder and (from the loops) harsher up high, deeper and smoother down low; toneHz: a low-pass that opens with the revs. intake: the air rushing in at high throttle, band-passed from hz[0] to hz[1] with the revs, heard from throttle[0]. shift: the clunk as a gear goes in. limiter: the cut each time the rev limiter cuts the fuel (at most every `every` s). damage: a blown engine's bang, bent valves' clack, and how far a misfire or valve float drops a firing (rough). The files are made from `synth` by npm run sounds (tools/content/sound.mjs); real recordings can replace them (same names, or new ones here) and synth can go.

synth._note: How npm run sounds makes the files (tools/content/sound.mjs). Pairs are [at idle, at the redline] (a layer's place between them by log rpm). Each firing: a pressure pulse (pulseRise, pulseDecay s, shorter up high) and combustion noise (noise × the pulse, noiseDecay s), cylinder to cylinder a little different (cylinders) and a little early or late (jitter, share of the gap); through the exhaust's resonances (band-passes: hz, q, gain on load, offLoad), plus direct × the raw pulse; high-passed at highpass Hz, driven into a soft clip (clip), low-passed at tone Hz; rms: the loop's level. Off load: the pulses × offLoad.pulse, some burble (random ± share per firing), its own noise, clip and tone.
